question: Why should student midwives use digital medical literature?

options.A: To base clinical decisions on current evidence
options.B: To find entertainment during night shifts
options.C: To avoid reading traditional midwifery textbooks
options.D: To replace hands-on training in the labor ward

explanation: Accessing digital literature helps midwives apply modern research findings to improve patient outcomes. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why should midwives look beyond casual web searches for clinical info?

options.A: Casual searches rarely provide reliable, peer-reviewed clinical guidelines
options.B: General websites are always too expensive to access
options.C: Search engines block all medical terminology by default
options.D: Standard browsers do not work on mobile phones

explanation: Casual searching often leads to unverified or outdated information, whereas clinical practice requires rigorous, peer-reviewed sources. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is a dedicated database for health literature?
explanation: PubMed is a well-known database maintained specifically for searching biomedical and health research articles. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h2)

question: How do bibliographic databases differ from general search engines?

options.A: General search engines never index medical articles
options.B: Databases focus strictly on peer-reviewed scholarly and clinical literature
options.C: Databases only work without an active internet connection
options.D: General search engines cost money to use while databases are free

explanation: Specialized databases filter out commercial blogs and general web pages to provide structured access to verified research. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which Boolean operator should you use when you want to broaden your search to include synonyms?
explanation: The OR operator tells the database to find articles containing at least one of the listed terms, increasing the number of results. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h3)

question: How do you search for postpartum hemorrhage while excluding caesarean sections?
explanation: Using the NOT operator allows the researcher to filter out studies that focus on the excluded term. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h3)

question: What does the acronym MeSH stand for in medical literature searching?
explanation: MeSH is the controlled vocabulary thesaurus used by PubMed to index biomedical articles consistently. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why use standardized subject headings instead of only free-text keywords?

options.A: It captures relevant articles even if authors use different synonyms for the same concept
options.B: It prevents the database from crashing during heavy internet traffic
options.C: It guarantees that every paper found is completely free to read
options.D: It automatically translates every article into the local language

explanation: Subject headings group different word variations under one standard term so important studies are not missed due to naming differences. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which study design sits near the top of the clinical evidence hierarchy?
explanation: Systematic reviews combine data from multiple clinical studies, providing the strongest level of reliable evidence. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is critical appraisal necessary when reviewing published medical research?

options.A: To prove that older textbooks are always completely incorrect
options.B: To format the bibliography according to institutional guidelines
options.C: To increase the citation count of the primary author
options.D: To determine if study methods are sound before changing clinical practice

explanation: Appraisal ensures that flaws in design or bias do not lead clinicians to adopt ineffective or unsafe practices. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h5)

question: What happens when digital medical sources are not properly cited in an assignment?
explanation: Using someone else's written work or research data without proper citation constitutes academic dishonesty known as plagiarism. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why is accurate referencing essential in clinical and academic writing?

options.A: It allows readers to verify the original evidence supporting a clinical claim
options.B: It guarantees that the research will receive funding approval
options.C: It eliminates the need for statistical data analysis in the paper
options.D: It prevents search engines from indexing the published paper

explanation: Clear citations maintain transparency and allow fellow clinicians to check the validity of the sources used. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h6)
